messages:
Maya: Heads-up — product asked if we can make traces for staging live a bit longer during feature rollouts. Current policy is 7d staging / 30d prod. Thinking about making staging 14d but cold-tiering sooner. Thoughts?
Jon: +1 on giving staging more buffer for rollouts, but cost is real. Any numbers on ingest delta?
Maya: Staging ingest is ~12% of prod on average, spikes when QA runs. Cost delta for 7->14d is ~18% on trace storage per month (back-of-envelope).
Taylor: If we extend staging TTL we should avoid hot storage retention; do hot for 3d then move to cold for the rest. Cold reads are rare.
Sam: Agreed. We also need to ensure queries from Console still hit hot cache for the active deployment window (canary -> general). Maybe keep a hot window pinned per-deployment via label?
Lina: Operational question — how do we implement per-deployment hot windows without exploding index cardinality? Per-deployment labels could add too many series.
Jon: We can use a bucketing strategy: active-deployments tag only for N most-recent rollouts, evict older ones. Use TTL-on-tag that expires after X days.
observability-bot: Note: retention-change runbook link: https://intra.redwood/ops/trace-retention-runbook :memo:
Taylor: Prototype config I sketched:
```yaml
retention:
  env_defaults:
    prod: {hot_days: 5, cold_days: 25}
    staging: {hot_days: 3, cold_days: 11}
  per_deployment_hot_window_days: 2
  dynamic_eviction_threshold: 2000 # spans/sec per service to keep hot
```
Sam: Two flags to watch: per_deployment_hot_window_days and dynamic_eviction_threshold. The dynamic threshold lets us push noisy services to cold earlier automatically.
Maya: Want to avoid surprises for teams. Recommend: expose a per-service dashboard that shows hot vs cold cost + a small alert when a service is auto-evicted from hot.
Lina: UX ask: Console should show "approximate query latency" from hot vs cold and a button to force-promote a deployment to hot (with approval flow).
Jon: Agree. Forcing hot should be gated (billing owner + infra). We don't want random product teams parking everything in hot.
Taylor: Implementation detail: exporter's backend needs to emit span.rollup metadata so cold store can still satisfy typical console queries (latency percentiles) without rehydrating full spans. That's extra ingest CPU but saves storage cost.
Sam: Also consider sampling policy layered on top: retain 100% of error-span traces for 30d, sample 10% of success traces into cold. Means users can still debug regressions.
Maya: Nice — error-preservation + aggressive success downsample is exactly what product wants. Lina can we add a small eval to confirm signal retention for our common SLOs?
Lina: Yes, will run a backtest over last 90d. If percentiles shift >2% we'll flag.
observability-bot: deploy-bot: retention-config updated in dev cluster by @Taylor at 1799993348 :white_check_mark:
Jon: One more thing — queries that span hot+cold need to be routed intelligently. If time range is within hot window route to hot store, otherwise split and merge results, but show a "mixed store" badge in Console.
Maya: Good call. Action items: Taylor to open PR for retention YAML + migration plan, Lina to run backtest, Sam to prototype auto-evict heuristics, Jon to spec gating for manual hot promotion. I'll collate into runbook and send to infra-review. :thumbsup:
Sam: SGTM
Taylor: PR started: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/7821
Lina: Backtest scheduled for tomorrow EOD
Maya: Thanks all — will loop in support if we need opt-ins for staging teams.
